title: OAuth self-signup role escalation via mass assignment
summary:
## Summary | Field | Value | | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Advisory ID** | GHSA-wqvf-7262-m7g8 | | **Package** | `beszel` (Hub, GitHub: `github.com/henrygd/beszel`) | | **Ecosystem** | Go / PocketBase web application (Docker) | | **Severity** | **Medium** | | **CVSS v3.1** | `5.4` (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N) | | **CWE** | CWE-915 (Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes)
CWE-269 (Improper Privilege Management) | | **CVE** | To be assigned (if maintainers disclose) | | **Affected** | Hub builds where `USER_CREATION=true` and an OAuth2/OIDC provider is enabled | | **Patched** | [f7fd3ef](https://github.com/henrygd/beszel/commit/f7fd3ef403085b64dc8a21a02011105b2251333a) | ## 1. Background Beszel Hub uses PocketBase as its data layer. When self-service OAuth/OIDC sign-up is enabled (`USER_CREATION=true`), a new OAuth user is supposed to get the regular `user` role. The sign-up path instead accepts attacker-controlled extra fields, and `users.role` is writable during OAuth record creation - so an attacker can self-assign `admin`. **Threat model.** The attacker must possess a genuine account at the configured OAuth/OIDC provider (this is **not** an authentication bypass). The impact is privilege escalation from `user` (self-service OAuth sign-up) to `admin`. ## 2. Description When `USER_CREATION=true`, Beszel allows OAuth2-based creation of `users` records using the rule: ```go cr := "@request.context = 'oauth2'" usersCollection.CreateRule = &cr ``` The OAuth2 `createData` payload can include writable user fields, including `role`. Since the `role` field accepts `admin`, an attacker registering a new OAuth2 account can supply `role: "admin"`. The default-role hook only assigns `user` when the role is empty: ```go if e.Record.GetString("role") == "" { e.Record.Set("role", "user") } ``` Therefore, an attacker-supplied `admin` value remains unchanged and is persisted to the new account. Beszel authorization subsequently trusts this stored value directly: ```go e.Auth.GetString("role") == "admin" ``` As a result, an unauthenticated attacker able to register through OAuth2 can create an administrative account and access admin-only functionality, including sensitive endpoints such as `/api/beszel/config-yaml`. ## 3. Reproduction ### 3.1 Prerequisites - Docker with Compose (v5.5+). - A checkout of the affected revision (verified: `6a7b2772`). - A local OIDC provider **or** any real OAuth2/OIDC provider. - This PoC uses the ready-made container `ghcr.io/navikt/mock-oauth2-server` so the stand runs fully offline (no external accounts). - Two OIDC identities: `control` (negative control) and `verify` (main check). ### 3.2 Expected result | Test | `createData` | Expected recorded `role` | | ------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------ | | Negative control | `{}` (no role) | `user`...

corrections.reason: The repository advisory writes the affected range as >= 0.9.0, <= 1.19.0 next to the patched version 0.20.0, a typo for 0.19.x: Beszel has never released a 1.x version. The fix commit f7fd3ef first shipped in 0.20.0, so 0.20.0 and later are not affected.
